lines: My fingers, swollen from soaking in water, meet.
Thinking it’s cold, I touch the chilly sky.
I trace the sky just like someone else.
The inside of my nose aches, cold and sharp.
My chest feels off, somehow uneasy.
What did I leave behind, what did I lose?
Becoming the tragic heroine is easy.
A solitary suspicion circles once more.
It grows and returns.
I don’t meet the eyes of my reflection.
I’m trying hard, someone watch me, acknowledge me.
Who am I saying that to? Hey, who am I saying it to?
Self‑questioning, self‑blame, blaming others, everything.
Again, I swallow everything without saying it out loud.
I’m an idiot.
Ridiculously foolish, disappointed in a god that doesn’t heal.
There’s nothing to do; if I’m wearing shoes, they’re big size.
Leaving footprints, breathing air into my lungs, I’m high.
If I reach out with this hand, the matching pair will appear instantly.
A world where even such exaggerated words can be spoken—nowhere.
Kick away this zero‑sum.
From my verse, I forge my own path.
Desperately turning the clock hands backward.
I’m struggling, I’m struggling (why).
My voice, a voice no one knows, is mine.
I’m here, I don’t understand, help me.
If I can’t even say it, at least, at least.
So I don’t miss even one.
I want only myself to understand me.
The empty bus seat beside me.
A one‑room I still don’t call home.
Blue light glowing in a dark room.
The roughness I felt with my hand.
Don’t ignore it.
I don’t meet the eyes of my reflection.
I’m trying hard, someone watch me, acknowledge me.
Who am I saying that to? Hey, who am I saying it to?
Self‑questioning, self‑blame, blaming others, everything.
Again, I swallow everything without saying it out loud.
My voice, a voice no one knows, is mine.
I’m here, I don’t understand, help me.
If I can’t even say it, at least, at least.
So I don’t miss even one.
I want only myself to understand me.
That’s why.
